approach: Add one required `dependents` list to PlanOutput and a defaulted-empty list on the JobPlan record. Refuse at admission in `plan_findings` (Major finding, so the plan goes back to the planner with no critic call) when the list is empty, or an entry has a blank `changed` or `dependent`, or has neither a test nor an unaffected-reason. planner.md requires the section and says to search by the behaviour the plan changes, not by the name of a new field. critic.md gains its own "what else does this change break" question that checks the list against a repository search. `plan_body` prints the list only when it is non-empty, so stored plans keep their producer-section hash. The CI-reuse replay now rebuilds the plan inputs as they were before the later fix. The changed item is "CheckRun.exit_code becomes None for CI-reused results". The test runs a real search of production code for readers of `exit_code` and requires it to find the seen-commands filter in verify.rs `judge`. It then runs real `plan_findings` on sections that omit and name verify.rs.

decisions.choice: The replay searches by the changed behaviour: non-comment, non-test lines in `crates/*/src/**/*.rs` that mention `exit_code`. It requires verify.rs to be hit on a line containing `exit_code == Some(0)`, the seen-commands filter that treats a missing exit code as not run.
decisions.reason: Finding 6. verify.rs:324 reads `c.exit_code == Some(0) || (c.reused && c.exit_code.is_none())`, and the `c.reused` arm is the later repair. A planner at the time of the CI-reuse change (HISTORY.txt 1b18983) had no `reused` field to search for. It could only search for what it changed: `exit_code` becoming None. A search on `exit_code` finds verify.rs both before and after the repair, so the replay reproduces the original plan inputs. Truncating each file at its first `#[cfg(test)]` line (verify.rs has it at line 628, after line 324) keeps test-only readers out.

rejected.why: It finds verify.rs only because the breakage was already repaired. It does not replay the original inputs.

rejected.option: Assert that a `.reused`-only search would have missed the rule before the fix
rejected.why: The pre-fix source is not in the snapshot, so the test would have to fake it. The changelog and design text state the lesson instead: search by the behaviour that changes, not by the new name.

decisions.choice: One flat list of entries `{changed, dependent, kind, test, unaffected_reason}`. `kind` is code, rule or host_setting.
decisions.reason: Each dependent needs its own test-or-reason, so one entry is the unit admission checks. It adds one schema object where nesting would add two. Nested object count in the schema test goes 5→6 (total objects 6→7), and the comment at outputs.rs:669 is updated to list `dependents` (finding 9).

rejected.option: Nested: a changed item holding a list of dependents
rejected.why: Two more object levels and a bigger record for the same information.
Admission could not name the dependent that lacks a test or reason, so the rule would be prose only.

decisions.choice: The check lives in `plan_findings` as Major findings: one at location 'dependents' for an empty list, and one per bad entry, naming the dependent.
decisions.reason: `plan_findings` is the pure, model-free check, and a Major finding already sends the plan back with no critic call. The rule is enforced by mechanism, not by prose alone.

rejected.why: A parse failure stops the job with 'no valid plan' instead of letting the planner revise.
Minor findings do not stop a plan.

decisions.choice: `PlanOutput.dependents` is required. `JobPlan.dependents` is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`, and `validate` does not demand it.
decisions.reason: New planner output must carry the section. Stored records without it must parse and re-serialize byte for byte. Only new plans are judged.

rejected.why: Two empty states for no gain.
The request says no new record file and no migration.
Scripted plans without it would parse and then fail admission anyway. An explicit field is clearer.

decisions.choice: `plan_body` prints a `Dependents:` block only when the list is non-empty.
decisions.reason: `render_plan_section` feeds `producer_section_sha256`, so an unconditional block would change the bytes of every stored plan. The producer, critic and revision briefs all use `plan_body`, so each shows the list.

rejected.why: It changes the hash input of every stored plan.

decisions.choice: The replay's 'section without verify.rs is unmet' step is the test's own comparison. The test says so, and so does the demonstration. Production behaviour is shown by the refusal of an incomplete verify.rs entry and by the briefs.rs test that renders the `Dependents:` block into `critic_brief`.
decisions.reason: Finding 7. Admission checks shape only, as the accepted reading says. Completeness against the search is the critic's job (brief) and the replay's. Calling `critic_brief` from the athena-core test would mean building the whole `CriticInputs` there, so the critic-path check lives in briefs.rs, next to `plan_body`.

rejected.why: `plan_findings` is pure with no repository access, and automatic dependency analysis is out of scope.

rejected.option: A production `unnamed_readers` function used only by tests

decisions.choice: The scope findings are handled this way. Drop docs/records.md. Keep docs/system-facts.md and the three CLI test files, and give the reason for each in the Files list. Leave refusal_corpus.rs without a case and add only a header note.
decisions.reason: Findings 1 to 5 and 8. The scripted plans in job_plan.rs, lifecycle.rs and introspection.rs are literal JSON that PlanOutput now requires, so they fail to parse without the field. `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` fails unless the two budget lines are updated. records.md is only optional accuracy, so it is cut. The refusal corpus runs `refusing_check` on readings. Its INPUT_FORMS list is all reading and request forms, and plan admission is not part of it. The listed deliverable is met by a header note that says where the plan-side rule is tested.

risks.risk: Several tests build JobPlan literals or scripted plan JSON. A missed one fails to compile or fails with 'no valid plan'.
risks.mitigation: Every literal site and scripted plan is listed in the steps. A missing struct field is a compile error, so `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` find any miss.

risks.risk: Changing plan_body alters the producer section hash of stored plans.
risks.mitigation: The block is printed only when non-empty. A briefs test asserts that a plan with no dependents renders the same text as before.

risks.risk: The prompt additions overflow the budgets (477 and 483 tokens left, ⌈bytes/3⌉), or the system-facts lines go stale.
risks.mitigation: Keep the additions near the sizes in the Files list, run the budgets test, and set the system-facts lines to the computed values.

risks.risk: The replay's `exit_code` search is brittle. It could match only non-seen-commands readers, or break if verify.rs is reorganised.
risks.mitigation: The test requires a verify.rs hit on a line containing `exit_code == Some(0)`, so a rename or move fails loudly rather than passing without meaning. Truncating each file at its first `#[cfg(test)]` line keeps test-only readers out.

risks.risk: Planners fill the section with boilerplate reasons.
risks.mitigation: A reason is an alternative to a test, so a truly unaffected dependent costs one line. The critic judges whether each reason is true against its own search.

demonstrations.method: Admission unit tests call the real `plan_findings` on a plan with no dependents section, on one whose entry has neither a test nor a reason (also whitespace-only), and on complete sections (test only, reason only, both). An end-to-end test in run/tests.rs scripts a first plan that lacks the section and checks that no Critic call is recorded before the second planner call.
demonstrations.observes: The empty list gives exactly one Major finding (source Athena) at location 'dependents' that names the missing section. The incomplete entry gives one Major finding whose location is 'dependents, <dependent>' and whose summary names it. Complete sections add no finding. The scripted run revises without a critic call.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check in `plan_findings` the empty and incomplete cases return no finding and the first two tests fail. The run/tests.rs test would see a Critic call after the first plan.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `plan_findings(&JobPlan, &Reading, &Policy, &dyn Fn(&str)->bool)` in crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs (exists, read). The fixture is a JobPlan literal in the admission test module, built like the existing `seam_findings` helper, with `dependents` varied and passed in directly. The end-to-end test uses `run_planned` with the scripted planner and the `bad_plan` / `good_plan` helpers in run/tests.rs (exist). Steps 4 and 5 add the field to those fixtures.

demonstrations.method: Test `ci_reuse_replay_requires_dependents_to_name_the_seen_commands_rule` in admission.rs replays the CI-reuse plan inputs as they were before the later fix. The plan modifies crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs. The changed item is 'CheckRun.exit_code becomes None for CI-reused results'. (1) It searches the real production sources, meaning `crates/*/src/**/*.rs` up to each file's first `#[cfg(test)]` line with comment lines skipped, for lines mentioning `exit_code`, and asserts the hits include verify.rs on a line containing `exit_code == Some(0)`. (2) A section naming only checks.rs and status.rs leaves that hit unnamed, so the test's own comparison reports the requirement unmet. (3) A section naming verify.rs `judge` seen-commands with a test gets no dependents finding from `plan_findings`. (4) The same verify.rs entry with no test and no reason gets a Major finding naming verify.rs.
demonstrations.observes: The search finds the seen-commands filter in verify.rs by `exit_code` alone, with no use of the later `reused` field. The section without verify.rs is reported unmet. The section with it is admitted. The incomplete verify.rs entry is refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the section does not name verify.rs, the step 2 assertion fails. If the seen-commands filter moves out of verify.rs or stops reading `exit_code`, step 1 fails. If `plan_findings` ignored dependents, step 4 fails. Step 2 is the test's own comparison and shows that the search finds the rule, not that admission refuses the section. Production refusal is shown by steps 3 and 4, and the critic path by the briefs.rs test in criterion 5.
demonstrations.seam: Production `plan_findings` in admission.rs (exists), driven by a JobPlan literal fixture that step 4 adds. The file search and the 'named or not' comparison are the test's own helpers, and they read the real sources, so verify.rs `judge` is the genuine rule. No model and no double. The fixture holds no logic under test.
